About us
Headquartered in San Francisco, California, Zeta was named by Celent in 2023 as being among the likeliest partners for US banks and credit unions looking to modernize to a next-gen issuer processing platform. With our marquee credit card ranked #2 by American cardholders, Zeta is already acknowledged by leading issuers as the go-to platform for market-leading credit card experiences. Globally, Zeta is recognized as a next-gen banking technology company. Our platform enables financial institutions to launch extensible and compliant banking asset and liability products, across cards, loans and deposits, rapidly. Our cloud-native and fully API-enabled stack supports processing, issuing, lending, core banking, fraud, loyalty, digital banking apps, and many other capabilities. Zeta has 1700+ employees with over 70% in technology roles across locations in the US, Middle East, and Asia, with regional headquarters in Mumbai, India. Globally, customers have issued 25M+ cards on our platform. Visit us at www.zeta.tech or follow us on LinkedIn, YouTube, and X.

2w

RuPay credit cards on UPI have solved one of digital payments' hardest problems- turning credit cards into an everyday payment tool. But the harder question now is whether the economics can keep pace with the engagement.
 
In Mint's latest feature on the RuPay-on-UPI story, Mehul Mistry, SVP, Customer Success, Strategy & Growth at Zeta, explains what the numbers reveal- RuPay cards linked to UPI are seeing 3.5 to 4 times as many monthly transactions as traditional cards, with a far lower average ticket size. The shift is moving credit cards from occasional big-ticket use to everyday spending.
 
As Mehul points out, the long-term upside for banks is not just migration from debit cards and bank-account UPI, but incremental credit consumption reaching merchant categories that historically saw little card usage at all.
 
Read the full feature here: https://lnkd.in/dMVnRka6
 
#RuPay #UPI #CreditCards #DigitalPayments #BankingInfrastructure #Fintech

RuPay-on-UPI boosts card usage, but profits remain elusive | Mint
RuPay-on-UPI boosts card usage, but profits remain elusive | Mint

4mo

The best customer relationships span products, channels, and time but most bank experiences today simply aren't built to nurture deep, long-term relationships. 

The gap exists because banks operate siloed systems, offer generic products without understanding customers’ lifestage, and deliver fragmented experiences across disconnected channels. The result is banking that feels transactional and impersonal—one-size-fits-all offerings instead of genuine relationships.

Join our panel discussion at CBA LIVE 2026 (Monday, March 30, 11:30 a.m. - 12:20 p.m.) as Matt C. (Regions Bank), T.J. Steele (Eastern Bank), Heather Warner (MX) and Shashank Mehrotra (Zeta) explore how to modernize relationship banking for a digital, AI-led world.

Add the session to your calendar today: 
https://lnkd.in/gNQzKdT5

#NextGenBankingTech #DigitalTransformation #CBALIVE2026

5mo

Digital payments have reached massive scale, and accountability must match it.

RBI's proposal to compensate up to ₹25,000 for small-value frauds marks an important shift toward stronger customer protection.
 
In ETBFSI, Mehul Mistry shares why fraud is rarely a single-point failure, and why a shared, system-wide approach is critical.

8mo

As agentic commerce moves from experiments to production, one issue keeps surfacing: the mechanics of trust in payments weren’t designed for software acting on our behalf.

That pressure is forcing issuers, networks, and processors to rethink basics we’ve long treated as solved: identity, consent, evidence, and where those controls live in the lifecycle. These are technical questions that directly shape fraud models, dispute operations, economics, and customer experience.

Gary Singh looks at how card infrastructure already contains most of the building blocks for governing autonomous transactions, and why wiring them to intent matters.

https://lnkd.in/gxWFmtcG

Card-First Agentic Payments: Making 'Intent' Safe on Today’s Rails
Card-First Agentic Payments: Making 'Intent' Safe on Today’s Rails

And that’s a wrap on three incredible days at GFF 2025. 

Our heartfelt thanks to Payments Council of India, National Payments Corporation Of India (NPCI), Fintech Convergence Council and the entire Global Fintech Fest team for bringing the ecosystem together so meaningfully.

It’s been an energizing few days - filled with ideas, conversations, and connections that reminded us how collaborative this industry truly is.

Our co-founders Bhavin Turakhia and Ramki Gaddipati sparked forward-looking conversations on the future of financial inclusion and the realities of AI in banking.

At the Zeta Pavilion, we created a space for the 𝘩𝘰𝘸 - where leaders paused for deeper, more candid discussions on turning vision into action.

To every leader, partner, and peer who made these three days special - thank you for the energy, insight, and intent you brought to every conversation.

Here’s a look back at a few moments that made this year’s GFF truly memorable.

Until next year!

10mo  Edited

The future of banking is being rewritten in code. 

Digital transformation is no longer a choice; it’s a competitive imperative. it’s the foundation on which the next decade of banking will be built.  
 
As institutions modernize their technology cores, they’re redefining how products are built, experiences are delivered, and scale is achieved. 

At this year’s Global Fintech Fest, Zeta CEO & Co-Founder Bhavin Turakhia spoke with NDTV Profit about how banks are embracing this shift — moving from legacy infrastructure to modern, cloud-native platforms that power speed, compliance, and innovation. 

As Bhavin puts it, “It’s no longer risky to go digital, it’s risky not to.” 

Watch his full conversation with NDTV Profit to explore how Zeta is helping banks accelerate into the future: https://lnkd.in/gJcVxjDM

As banks accelerate their technology refresh projects, Zeta stands out as the preferred full-stack partner delivering modern, scalable, and compliant technology at speed.

Our partnerships with top-tier banks have demonstrated how next-gen core systems for payments, cards, and digital banking can together scale seamlessly on a single platform.

In a discussion with Mint, at this year’s Global Fintech Fest, Zeta Co-founders, Bhavin Turakhia and Ramki Gaddipati shared how Zeta is shaping the future of digital banking in India and beyond.

With steady growth and strong traction in India, across credit cards, UPI, and digital payments, Zeta is gearing up for its next phase of expansion.
